title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction (v2)
shortDescription: CKP signal fault detected; PCM cannot establish reliable engine timing reference.
fullDescription: CKP signal fault detected; PCM cannot establish reliable engine timing reference. Without a clean position pulse the spark and injector timing references drift, leading to no-start, hard-start or stalling events. Air-gap, reluctor damage and harness chafe near hot exhaust components are typical root causes.
safetyImpact: Stalling at speed removes power steering / power brake assist; investigate before continued use.

causes.cause: Crankshaft Position Sensor failed
Reluctor / tone wheel damaged or contaminated
Sensor air gap out of spec
Wiring chafe near exhaust manifold or block
Loose timing chain causing phase drift

symptoms: Stalling at idle or under load

fixSteps.title: Scan-data review
fixSteps.instruction: Capture CKP RPM signal and compare to crankshaft RPM during a cranking event. Drop-outs indicate signal loss.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness and connector
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe sensor connector; check 5V reference, ground, and signal return. Wiggle harness to provoke fault.

fixSteps.title: Measure sensor resistance / air gap
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor resistance to spec (typically 200-1000 ohms for variable reluctance). Set air gap with feeler gauge.

fixSteps.title: Inspect reluctor wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor and inspect reluctor teeth for missing teeth, debris or runout. Replace as needed.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Short trips at low load may be possible, but stalling can occur without warning. Repair before highway driving.

faq.q: Is the timing chain related?
faq.a: A stretched chain can phase the camshaft enough to log this code. Inspect chain stretch first on high-mileage engines.

Without a clean position pulse the spark and injector timing references drift, leading to no-start, hard-start or stalling events. Air-gap, reluctor damage and harness chafe near hot exhaust components are typical root causes.
safetyImpact: Stalling at speed removes power steering / power brake assist; investigate before continued use.

causes.cause: Camshaft Position Sensor failed
Reluctor / tone wheel damaged or contaminated
Sensor air gap out of spec
Wiring chafe near exhaust manifold or block
Loose timing chain causing phase drift

symptoms: Stalling at idle or under load

fixSteps.title: Scan-data review
fixSteps.instruction: Capture CMP RPM signal and compare to crankshaft RPM during a cranking event. Drop-outs indicate signal loss.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness and connector
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe sensor connector; check 5V reference, ground, and signal return. Wiggle harness to provoke fault.

fixSteps.title: Measure sensor resistance / air gap
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor resistance to spec (typically 200-1000 ohms for variable reluctance). Set air gap with feeler gauge.

fixSteps.title: Inspect reluctor wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor and inspect reluctor teeth for missing teeth, debris or runout. Replace as needed.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Short trips at low load may be possible, but stalling can occur without warning. Repair before highway driving.

faq.q: Is the timing chain related?
faq.a: A stretched chain can phase the camshaft enough to log this code. Inspect chain stretch first on high-mileage engines.

title: Cylinder 301 Misfire Detected (Extended) (EXT)
shortDescription: PCM detects abnormal crankshaft acceleration variance attributable to cylinder 301.
fullDescription: PCM detects abnormal crankshaft acceleration variance attributable to cylinder 301. Random misfires across multiple cylinders point to fuel, vacuum, or compression issues; isolated single-cylinder misfires usually mean a coil, plug or injector problem on that bank.
safetyImpact: Sustained misfires can melt the catalytic converter; do not drive flashing-MIL.

causes.cause: Worn spark plug on cylinder 301
Failed coil-on-plug
Fuel injector clogged or shorted
Low compression / leaking valve
Vacuum leak at intake runner

fixSteps.title: Swap coil and plug
fixSteps.instruction: Move the coil and plug from cylinder 301 to a known-good cylinder. If misfire follows, replace the failed component.

fixSteps.title: Compression test
fixSteps.instruction: Test all cylinders dry then wet. A 15%+ deviation indicates ring or valve sealing problem.

fixSteps.title: Injector balance test
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scan tool to disable each injector and watch RPM drop. The weak cylinder will show a smaller drop.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test intake
fixSteps.instruction: Smoke-test the intake manifold for vacuum leaks at runner gaskets and PCV passages.

faq.q: Can I just keep driving?
faq.a: Brief low-load driving is OK but a flashing CEL means active catalyst damage. Stop and tow if it flashes.

faq.q: What if I changed plugs and coils and it still misfires?
faq.a: Move to compression and injector tests; mechanical or fuel-side issues mimic ignition misfire.
